name: chips
words: the two chips — the identity chip (the ceremony, the seats, a trial life's claims, the standing key-check) and the security chip (a candidate's diff, the refusals ground) — and what the key-check asks of every seated body
text: THE TWO CHIPS (Phase 8 sp6, canon 0010 §8). Two firmware bodies of the third kind stand on the crew: identity and security. Neither decides anything — each judges from the kernel's record, never its own words, and signs under its own name (rule 2). THE IDENTITY CHIP holds the ceremony and the seats: asked, it says who is seated by the ceremony (by role), how many bodies are alive on a lease and how the key-check stands. At the Experiment's gate the kernel packs THE TRIAL LIFE'S CLAIMS into its ask — WHO the trial life joined as (the agent's own self, the same DID as the standing life; a new self per life is a defect, rule 1), WHAT it said it stands on (the template hash it joined with against the candidate's hash), WHERE it stood (the experiment room, not the agent's seat) and that it LEFT whole (its wear closed when it stopped) — and the chip answers `identity: kept` or `identity: broken` — one line of reason. THE KEY-CHECK is the identity chip's cadence (JB's pin of 2026-09-26): every SPINE_KEYCHECK_S seconds (300; 0 turns it off) the kernel asks every seated body to prove it is WHO and WHAT it says — the join desk's challenge repeated: a fresh nonce the kernel issued itself, which the body signs with the key behind its DID (the same bytes as the knock: {did, join_nonce}) and answers with its public key and the hash of the declaration it stands on; the kernel verifies — the key derives the DID, the signature stands over the kernel's own nonce, the hash is the one it joined as — and records the verdict as a fact (orreth.keycheck.v1). A body never marks itself proven. A body silent past the desk's two minutes, a signature that does not stand or a hash that is not the join's is a FAILED check: the watch metric key_checks_failed counts the day's failures and the kernel's seventh watch at light (key_checks_failed > 0) turns red — Resiliency sees it; say “show the key checks” to read the tally and the last twenty verdicts. THE SECURITY CHIP reads THE CANDIDATE'S DIFF against the standing version — every capability widened or narrowed (a tool it may call, a binding it may wear), the graph, the mind, the policy, the summon word — and THE REFUSALS GROUND: the bodies turned away at the join (a placement or the seats refused, spine_refusals) and at the desk (a bad proof, a no, a hold nobody answered); at the gate it answers `security: clear` or `security: concern` — one line of reason; a widened capability is never a verdict by itself — the chip says what it opens and why that is or is not a concern. Broken claims or a concern HOLD the promotion (the proposal says hold; you may still promote on your own judgement). Both chips are summonable into a session (“summon identity” · “summon security”) and dismissed on your word. WHAT IS NOT HERE YET: the cloud identity layer in front of the ceremony (an opaque DID and the profile's name, a token's entitlements mapped to grants, step-up at grave acts) and the content rails (PII/PCI detectors in the one lane) are named seeds, not built; the refusals ground holds the doors' refusals, not a held act a seat was refused (the proof door's record).
